text:
Pete L.: quick follow-up from the MHA RFC meeting — we've got two pressing questions folks: should runtime expose an abstracted 'QKV layout' enum (NHWC/NCHW/INTERLEAVED/PLANAR) or just stride/shape descriptors?
Anya K.: my vote is enum + stride fallback. enums let kernel selector short-circuit fastpaths, strides handle oddball hardware quirks.
Jia R.: agree. enums are great for optimization heuristics, but we still need a canonical internal for cached KV storage. contig QKV (interleaved) helps streaming and cache locality.
Kevin M.: note: contiguous interleaved QKV wins on throughput for fused matmul+softmax kernels (see perf-bot micro run). but it complicates tensor transforms when we need per-head quantization.
perf-bot: microbench summary 
  model: bert-base-like, seqlen 64, heads 12, d_k 64
  layout=INTERLEAVED (qkv packed) => +18% throughput vs PLANAR on A100 80GB
  layout=NHWC (qkv separate but channel-last) => +6% lower latency for seqlen<=32
  caveat: mixed-precision path regresses if per-head scales differ
Sara (eng-runtime): one constraint we didn't highlight: KV cache API must remain stable across model rollouts. if we change memory layout, we need a migration or dual-path decode. can't break live sessions.
Pete L.: right — two practical routes: 1) ABI-level descriptor: (layout_enum, strides[], head_dim, packed_qkv_bool) that kernels read and choose implementation, or 2) abstract ops that normalize into runtime canonical buffer before kernel (extra memcpy).
Anya K.: option 1 is nicer for perf but increases kernel complexity and testing matrix. option 2 simpler but adds copy latency and memory pressure for large batch sizes.
Jia R.: also consider partial packing: pack Q and K together but leave V planar; some of our workloads mostly hit QK attention so we get most wins with less mutation.
Kevin M.: thinking about kernel selector flags: prefer implementing "fastpath" predicates like: is_contiguous_packed && head_dim % 8 == 0 && seqlen <= 128. If true, use fused kernel. Otherwise fallback to generic.
Pete L.: +1. we should encode those predicates in a declarative table so scheduler can reason about cost. avoids hardcoding heuristics in multiple places.
Sara (eng-runtime): ops API proposal (WIP):
```
OpDesc {
  shape: [B, S, H, D],       // explicit dims
  layout: "INTERLEAVED"|"PLANAR"|"NHWC"|"NCHW",
  strides: [..],
  packed_qkv: boolean,
  head_dim: int,
  dtype: "fp16"|"bf16"|"int8",
}
```
Kernels register which layouts/strides they support. runtime picks best match.
Anya K.: question: do we keep legacy NHWC/NCHW names? some folks conflate NHWC with channel-last packing which isn't identical to 'packed_qkv'. maybe rename to CHANNEL_LAST / CHANNEL_FIRST + PACKING hints.
Jia R.: name bikeshedding aside, we also need a migration story for Dedicated customers using pinned model binaries. propose: default runtime will accept both old and new descriptors and expose a "compat_mode" toggle at deployment level to force legacy transforms.
Kevin M.: one more perf note: stride aliasing kills vectorized kernels. if a tensor has non-unit inner stride we should prefer a copy to a contiguous buffer for the fastpath — but only when predicted token count * batch > threshold. perf-bot can compute the threshold heuristically.
perf-bot: added threshold table to issue #412: contiguous-copy payback = 3.4ms at batch*seqlen=4096 for A100 fp16 fused kernel.
Pete L.: action items:
- Anya: draft OpDesc PR with enum + strides + packed_qkv examples (ETA Tue)
- Jia: run perf sweep for partial-packing (Q+K packed, V planar) across seqlen [8,16,32,64,128] on p4d/p3 (ETA Fri)
- Kevin: prototype kernel selector predicate table + integration tests (ETA next Wed)
- Sara: write compatibility doc for Dedicated customers and add flag to deployment config (ETA Thu)
Anya K.: ack. I'll include sample mem layout diagrams and a small conversion snippet.
Jia R.: will try to reduce noise in metrics by attaching per-run standard deviation.
Kevin M.: ping me if you need matrix expansion help.
Pete L.: thanks all. if nobody objects I'll merge the RFC follow-up notes into the runtime repo after PRs land. :thumbsup:
